title: The same reason then
hookLine: don't be troubled by the future; you'll meet it with the same reason you have now (Meditations 7.8)
carry: the same you, with the same tools

cards: It's 2am. The house is quiet, and your mind is running a movie of next month. The meeting where it all goes wrong.
The bill you can't pay. The phone call from the doctor. You play it three different ways, and in every version you're alone and unprepared.
Here's the strange thing: in the movie, the person facing the future is a weaker, more confused version of you. Somehow we imagine that when the hard day comes, we'll show up with nothing.
Marcus had a short answer to 2am.

teach.h: LET NOT FUTURE THINGS DISTURB THEE.
teach.b: Book Seven, section eight, in George Long's translation: "Let not future things disturb thee, for thou wilt come to them, if it shall be necessary, having with thee the same reason which now thou usest for present things."
Three pieces. First: let not future things disturb you. Not: the future won't be hard.
It might be. Just: don't let it trouble you now.
Second: if it shall be necessary. Some of what we dread never arrives. Marcus doesn't promise that, but he leaves the door open.

teach.h: THE SAME REASON YOU USE NOW.
teach.b: Third, the heart of it: you'll bring with you the same reason you're using today. Reason, for the Stoics, meant more than logic. It meant the whole power in you to see clearly, choose well and act rightly.
And it's portable. Whatever you use today to handle the dishes, the emails and the hard conversation, you'll have tomorrow too. The 2am movie always forgets this.
It sends a helpless you into the future.
Marcus says it'll be the same you, with the same tools, and probably more practice. That gathers up our week of seeing clearly. The purple robe was only outward show.
The emperor refused to be dyed a Caesar. The bee belongs to the hive. Our palms are small on the elephant.
The call was already the answer. The dragon was only frozen. And the future is met by the same mind you have now.
Your line: the same you, with the same tools.

how: Many readers of the Stoics use this line at night or in anxious moments, reminding themselves that the same judgment and care they have today will be there when the future arrives.

games.why: let not future things disturb you: you'll come to them with the same reason you use today.

practice: Let one worry about the future come up, and look at it once. Picture yourself on that day with the same mind and the same care you have right now, maybe with a friend beside you, and say inside: I'll meet it then.
Set it down, and if it comes back, just say it again.

wordCard.voice: Reason. For the Stoics, the whole power in you to see clearly, choose well and act rightly, carried with you into whatever future comes. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: reason, word, account. the Stoics' word for the reasoning power in us, and in the universe.

carryVoice: Your line: the same you, with the same tools. A week of seeing clearly, complete. See you tomorrow.
